authoredNote: Authored BEFORE the `instantiates` reading landed, so the pre-change run is a FAILING run (5 expected `instantiates` edges, 0 actual) and a regression is visible. Line numbers are the BLOCK HEADER lines the TYPE label is written on (8, 13, 17, 22, 36), transcribed from the numbered source; every block's first label is the type, the second is the instance name, and only the TYPE is a target.
rationale: `instantiates` is the construction relation: a `resource` / `data` block builds an instance of the PROVIDER TYPE its first label names. Terraform's type is declared by a provider BINARY, in no repository, so the whole admitted corpus (3,932 resource/data blocks over 444 distinct type labels) contains ZERO labels declared as an address anywhere — measured, and recorded as the corpus-unexercised fact under HCL-D13, not used as a reason to publish nothing. The edge's SOURCE is the declaring file's root-module symbol (the document owns the block) and its TARGET is the type label AS WRITTEN (`aws_instance`), which is symbol-shaped and deliberately NOT a declaration the analyzer invents: no symbol is created for a provider type, and the target resolves externally/unresolved exactly as the contract requires. `metadata.instanceType` carries the label, `metadata.instanceKind` says whether the block is a `resource` or a `data` source, and `metadata.instanceName` carries the block's second label so a consumer can tell which instance was constructed. The near misses are pinned as FORBIDS because each is a different fact: a nested block (`lifecycle`, `dynamic`/`content`) is a MEMBER of its enclosing declaration and names no type (already `contains`), a `module` block names a SOURCE (already `imports`, and a module is a separate unit, never an instantiation of one — HCL-D11), a `variable` declares a value, and a variable's `type = list(number)` constraint is a type EXPRESSION, not a construction of a declared type.
